newsitem.title: USA: US Midcontinent diesel diffs ease in Group Three.
newsitem.headline: US Midcontinent diesel diffs ease in Group Three.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot low sulphur diesel basis eased in Group Three but buyers were beginning to re-emerge in the market, which could firm differentials on Thursday, traders said.

Trade in the Group Three and Chicago markets was being driven by the Merc, where front-month heating oil and unleaded gasoline futures had posted gains of about one cent a gallon in late-afternoon trade.
"There were more sellers than buyers yesterday," one trader said of the drop in Group Three diesel differentials. "But I'm talking to some buyers right now."
"The cash market deflated yesterday," a Group Three trader said.
Colder weather in the upper Midwest region heated up high sulphur diesel interest as trade began to wind down in November deliveries ahead of Thanksgiving week, a Chicago trader said.
"Nothing's going to get done next week, it's going to be real quiet, so a lot of guys are getting positions taken care of now," the Chicago trader said.

Group Three low sulphur diesel differentials fell below the print, easing to 0.75/0.50 cent a gallon under NYMEX December heating oil for prompt deliveries and 1.0/0.75 cent under for later deliveries.
Group Three unleaded was talked 3.25/3.50 cents a gallon over the print for prompt deliveries and firmed to 2.25/2.50 cents over for later deliveries.
